children.value: > Fact From Story: The Arab Center for Social Media Advancement (7amleh) told TechCrunch it has received reports of Instagram inconsistently filtering comments containing the Palestinian flag emoji.
> > Fact From Story: Users report that Instagram has flagged comments containing the emoji as “potentially offensive,” hiding the comment.

> > > Fact From Story: Jalal Abukhater said that the organization has documented multiple cases of journalists on Instagram reporting the same news in Arabic, Hebrew and English, but only getting flagged for their Arabic content.
> > > Commonsense Knowledge: Journalistic content should not be censored based on the language it is written in.
> > Commonsense Knowledge: Hiding comments makes them less visible to other users.

> Fact From Story: During the last violent outbreak between Hamas and Israel in 2021, a report commissioned by Meta and conducted by a third party concluded that the company’s actions had an “adverse human rights impact” on Palestinian users’ right to freedom of expression and political participation.

> > Fact From Story: Meta forbids support of terrorist organizations, like most social media companies based in the U.S., but struggles to moderate content around it, from user discourse to journalistic updates.
> > Commonsense Knowledge: Moderation policies should be applied without bias.
> Commonsense Knowledge: Selectively filtering content based on political expression displays moderation bias.
